messages.author: 693670b12cd395ae
messages.subject: BootstrapLRT() interpretation of output
parts:
Dear all,

I am exploring the use of the function bootstrapLRT() in the context of invariance testing. Concretely, I compared a restricted (metric invariance, i.e., equal loadings across groups) to an unrestricted (configural invariance, i.e., all parameters freely estimated across groups) model using bootstrapLRT, like this:

bootstrapLRT(load_invariant_model,configural_model)

My question is: what's the output of this function?

I assume it is the... p-value of the Likelikood Ratio Test (i.e., difference in Chi-Squares). But this p-value is based on the estimated distribution of the LRT across 1000 bootstrapped samples? 
Not sure if this is correct, because it feels like this interepretation is not very clearly stated in the help page for the function? (especially since there's not "Value" section) If anybody could confirm this interpretation, or point out to where I could find the answer, that would be very helpful.

Thank you very much!

Carlos

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: BootstrapLRT() interpretation of output
parts:
what's the output of this function?

I assume it is the... p-value of the Likelikood Ratio Test
It is.  Optionally, you can set return.LRT=TRUE if you want the empirical distribution of LRT stats as well.
this p-value is based on the estimated distribution of the LRT across 1000 bootstrapped samples?

Yes, it is the proportion of bootstrap samples with at least as large a LRT stat as the one from the original data.
 
Not sure if this is correct, because it feels like this interpretation is not very clearly stated in the help page for the function? (especially since there's not "Value" section)

I agree, I just pushed a change to correct that omission: https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/pull/233
